QQQ.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
QQQ’s 252-return DFA H was 0.480 on Nov 24, near the independent finite-variance reference of 0.5. R²=0.925 measures fit only at supplied scales. Short/long estimates (0.400/0.525) indicate one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Absolute-return H=0.758 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H fell from 0.520 on Nov 6 but rose 0.004/0.015 over 1/5 observations. Its prior-30 z-score was −0.08; overlapping windows preclude significance testing with this score.

Hill alpha fell from 3.50 on Nov 19 to 3.27 on Nov 23–24. Unchanged extremes can explain plateaus. The 1,000-return fit uses k=100 and x_min=0.02051 absolute log-return units. Lower alpha suggests heavier tails if the model fits. Independent-return SE=0.327 understates uncertainty with dependence. The 5%/15% cutoffs yield 3.27/2.98, not confidence limits. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.

SPY.source: Yahoo Finance via yfinance (unofficial provider client)

interpretation.text:
SPY’s 252-return DFA H was 0.499, near the independent finite-variance reference (0.5). R²=0.952 measures fit only at tested scales. Short/long estimates (0.379/0.555) differ: one line fits poorly across scales 8–63, possibly reflecting crossover or a temporary volatility shift. Magnitude H=0.709 suggests volatility clustering, not tradable predictability.

H rose 0.0030/0.0037 over 1/5 observations. The prior-30 standardized deviation was +0.13, not a significance test because windows overlap. H/alpha moved from 0.527/3.400 (Nov 6) to 0.499/3.183 (Nov 24).

Hill uses 1,000 returns (~4 years), with k=99 and x_min=0.01461 in absolute log-return units. Lower/higher alpha suggests heavier/thinner tails if the model fits. The idealized independent-return standard error (0.320) understates uncertainty under dependence. The 5%/15% cutoff estimates (3.085/2.820) aren’t confidence bounds. Alpha’s Nov 23–24 plateau can occur when the top extremes stay unchanged, not because the market is static. These are uncertain descriptive estimates, not a crash forecast.
